Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with rapidly enlarging lip swelling and subjective dyspnea after prawn exposure, with concern for anaphylaxis; ambulance advised and antihistamines to be used if available; follow-up planned after hospital assessment.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lip swelling after consuming a prawn-containing item (prawn soup) about 7:00 PM; initial lip swelling on the left corner, now progressing to the upper lip and increasing in size; associated sensation of throat tightness and difficulty breathing; patient reports dizziness.
- Timeline: Exposure around 7:00 PM; swelling developed within about 30 minutes and has been increasing; currently worrisome with breathing difficulties; ambulance requested.
- Exacerbating/initiating/relieving factors: Prawn-containing food as trigger; no mentioned relief yet.
- Associated symptoms: Throat tightness, breathing difficulty, dizziness; chest tightness uncertain but possible.
- Past medical history: Asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler); peanut allergy.
- Past similar episodes: About a year ago, after a late-night Chinese meal with curry-type dish; experienced swelling and difficulty breathing the next morning; treated with inhaled salbutamol; details unclear.
- Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (regular use) documented; other inhalers not listed.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy documented.
- Social history: Not explicitly detailed beyond current event; prior social activity with friends noted.
- Family history: Not mentioned.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma.
- Peanut allergy.
- Prior episode of facial swelling with breathing difficulty around age ~6 years (self-reported); details limited.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (regular use); dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:

Investigations:

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected anaphylactic reaction to prawn exposure.
  - Plan:
    - Activate emergency medical services and arrange urgent transport to the hospital (ambulance advised).
    - Interim management: Have antihistamines available and administer if accessible (patient’s mother to provide/coordinate).
    - Advise avoidance of further exposure to shellfish/prawns while awaiting EMS.
    - Post-hospital follow-up: Contact the clinic after discharge to arrange evaluation and discussion of future management, including possible injections (epinephrine) as indicated.
